summary: Atlus and Racdym/Racjin's kart-like snowboarding series; use Nintendo 64 for the original two games and Nintendo DS hardware/emulation for SBK.

entries.title: Snowboard Kids
entries.definitive_edition: Nintendo 64 original, with PlayStation Plus port as comparison

emulation.emulator: Nintendo 64 emulator / DuckStation for PlayStation comparison
emulation.notes: Use N64 route for primary multiplayer preservation.

primary.why: The original Snowboard Kids was built for Nintendo 64 with four-player racing; the Japan-only PlayStation version is an enhanced port, but no specific must-play exclusive content over the N64 route is known.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo 64 hardware or a local N64 emulator with four-controller support; sample Snowboard Kids Plus on PlayStation only for port comparison.

all_releases.fidelity: Original N64 release with up-to-four-player racing.
Japan-only enhanced port titled Snowboard Kids Plus.
all_releases.reason: skip: interesting port comparison, but no sourced exclusive content is asserted for a required secondary playthrough.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PlayStation has an enhanced Japan-only port, but the N64 original is the clearer multiplayer preservation route.

emulation.notes: Use original hardware or accurate N64 emulation.

primary.why: Snowboard Kids 2 is a Nintendo 64-only sequel with story mode, hub-town structure, battle mode, boss stages, and 15 courses.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo 64 hardware or a local N64 emulator with four-controller support.

emulation.notes: Use original DS/3DS hardware for local wireless multiplayer.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native DS or high-resolution DS emulation

primary.why: SBK is the Nintendo DS-only third and final Snowboard Kids game, with wireless multiplayer and a hidden Jack Frost/Black Frost Atlus cameo route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo DS/3DS hardware for local wireless play, or use melonDS/DeSmuME for single-player preservation.

all_releases.fidelity: Original DS release with wireless multiplayer support.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: DS hardware best preserves local wireless play; emulation improves display output but may not preserve multiplayer behavior.
